signals.text: All children, including PP and SEND, are given the chance to attend varied clubs, for example dodgeball, boys’ football, girls’ football, foot tennis and tennis.
Activity/Action Impact Comments The funding was spent on a range of resources, a PE coach to offer a wider range of sport/PE for our pupils, as well as give CPD opportunities for staff.
PE lessons and training in clubs from teachers and parents allows children to compete in football, cross country, netball, athletics and cricket competitively.

signals.text: All children, including PP and SEND, are given the chance to attend varied clubs, for example dodgeball, boys’ football, girls’ football, foot tennis and tennis.
Key responsibilities include: ● Oversees identification of SEND, including early screening, monitoring progress, and ensuring high-quality teaching and interventions.

Pupils who have an Education Health Care Plan (EHCP) or who require an EHCP By referral only Adapted lessons for pupils with SEN/D Access to ICT provision: interactive whiteboard (IWB), laptops, ipads, Bikeability: In Years 5 & 6.
High - quality, adaptive teaching and assessment underpin our curriculum, with reasonable adjustments made so every learner can access learning and develop cultural capital.

Special educational provision is defined as support that is additional to or different from that provided for pupils of the same age, and addresses needs across four areas: Cognition and Learning; Communication and Interaction; Physical and Sensory; and So cial, Emotional and Mental Health.

Achieving Believing Caring
Welcome
It is a great pleasure to welcome you to St Lawrence C of E (A) Junior school. I am incredibly proud to be the headteacher of such a thriving and happy school where our children demonstrate values of ‘Achieving, Believing and Caring’ every day. Our children are supported in becoming confident and independent young people, who thrive on challenge, and are motivated to learn.

pageCache.pageTitle: St Lawrence CofE Aided Junior School - Governors' Fund
pageCache.text:
Governors' Fund
Governors' Fund
The Governor’s Fund is at the heart of many of the improvements that make our school a vibrant, modern, and welcoming place to learn. Thanks to the generosity of our families and community, we are able to go beyond the basics and provide facilities and resources that truly make a difference.
Your support has already had a powerful impact. Most recently, the fund enabled us to provide brand-new computers for all staff, ensuring our teachers have the up-to-date technology they need to deliver inspiring and effective lessons every day.
We have also enhanced our school’s facilities by refurbishing the entrance toilet, transforming it into a fully accessible disabled toilet. This important upgrade supports our inclusive ethos and allows access outside school hours—making it ideal for community use when hiring our MUGA (Multi-Use Games Area) and school field.
Looking to the future, we are excited to be upgrading to energy-efficient LED lighting this summer. This project reflects our commitment to sustainability while continuing to improve our environment for pupils, staff, and visitors alike.
This fund also supports the school's teaching of the curriculum and helps meet the cost of providing experiences for pupils that greatly enhance the learning environment at St Lawrence.
Every contribution to the Governor’s Fund helps bring these projects to life. Together, we are building a better school for our children and our wider community.
👉 Donate Now
If you have not already set up a monthly donation, we warmly invite you to support the Governor’s Fund and help us continue making a real difference. No contribution is too small—every donation goes directly towards improving our school.
Have a look at the photos below to see the difference your support is making!

pageCache.pageTitle: St Lawrence CofE Aided Junior School - Clubs
pageCache.text:
Clubs
In addition to our own Breakfast Club and "Come and Play" After-School Club, we are pleased to be able to offer a wide variety of extra-curricular activities here at St Lawrence, both before and after school hours and at lunchtimes, making the most of our great facilities.
Activities on offer may change from time to time, depending on what staff and other organisations are able to offer and on what is appropriate to the time of year. We have a mixture of free and paid-for clubs, run by our own staff and by outside agencies. Each club will usually take bookings for, and run for, a term at a time.
Externally run clubs
Many of the activities on offer are run by external companies and must be booked directly with the company concerned. Clicking on the appropriate link in the schedule below will give you all the information you need to book your child into a particular club. Additionally, we will send out information about the available clubs via ParentMail.
Please be aware that the school is not responsible for the safety and security of children before the gates are opened at 8:30am. Children attending clubs before that time must be accompanied to the club by a responsible adult, not dropped at the school gate. It is the responsibility of those running the club to inform parents and carers of any changes or cancellations and the school will not provide alternative care arrangements in the event of a club not running. Similarly, if your child is not attending a club or you need to make special arrangements, please contact the club directly. The school office will not be able to pass on messages to individual clubs.
School Clubs
For school led clubs, you will be notified when the booking for the club is open (before the start of each new term) and will be directed to pay via ParentMail.
